title: Why Lipstick Survives When Money Gets Tight
title_options: The Lipstick Effect: Why Small Luxuries Survive Tight Budgets
Can Lipstick Sales Predict a Recession? Not Reliably
Why Small Luxuries Survive When Bigger Ones Get Cut
description: Why can a tiny luxury survive when money gets tight? The lipstick effect describes how tighter budgets can push bigger indulgences aside while a smaller comfort such as lipstick still feels affordable. Juliet Schor described this behavior in 1998, and Leonard Lauder popularized the “lipstick index” in 2001, suggesting lipstick sales might rise when the economy weakens. Later downturns did not repeat that pattern reliably, so lipstick sales are not a dependable economic indicator. “Lipstick syndrome” is also not a recognized medical diagnosis; here it is an informal label for small comforts under pressure. Q Station is an educational channel where every question opens a world. #LipstickEffect #ConsumerBehavior #Economics
